sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Collect tag requests
sections.what: Runs from a manual trigger or from request files pushed to the working or main branch. It gathers the requested tag names and commit ids into one list.
sections.why: The header says the agent's git proxy refuses tag pushes, so this workflow does the work.
sections.watch_out: On push, only added or changed request files are read, so a file deleted in the same push creates nothing.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Validate and create tags
sections.what: Checks each name is either a gate from 0 to 7 or a version number, checks the commit is real and reachable from the working or main branch, and refuses to move an existing tag. Then it creates the annotated tag and its reference. A tag already on the right commit is skipped.
sections.why: The header says names are limited and commits must be reachable, and a tag on a different commit fails the run.
sections.watch_out: The name pattern is strict, so any new naming style must be added to the pattern before a tag can be created.

summary: Creates tags (fixed names on commits) for approved names and commits, so the agent can mark milestones through GitHub.
purpose: Let tags be created without the agent pushing them directly.
why: The header says the agent's git proxy refuses tag pushes, so this workflow creates them with the workflow token. The strict name rules keep tags to project gates and versions.
how: 1) Collect requests from manual inputs or changed request files. 2) Merge them into one list. 3) For each one, check the name, check the commit exists, check it is reachable from the main branches, and check any existing tag. 4) Create the annotated tag and its reference. 5) Report each result.
inputs: Manual inputs (tag, commit id, message) or request files under data/requests/tags.
outputs: Annotated tags on GitHub and a log line for each tag.
risks: Tags are hard to remove cleanly once others rely on them. The write permission covers repository contents.
debug: A refusing tag name message means the name is outside the allowed pattern. An exists at another commit message means the tag was made earlier. If nothing happens, check that the request file was added or changed in the push.
